models.blurb: deepseek-v4.1-flash 1mo cloud Designed for greater capability, faster inference, higher throughput, and scaling to larger models. 1M $ $ $ $
models.name: Designed for greater capability, faster inference, higher throughput, and scaling to larger models.
models.description: Readme DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash: Pushing the Limits of KV Cache Compression DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash is an advanced tool designed to enhance search capabilities, providing users with faster and more accurate results. It’s a multimodal Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) model with 552B backbone parameters and support for contexts of up to one million tokens. DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash uses a Causal Encoder-Decoder (CED) design, stacking a 20-layer causal encoder on top of a 20-layer decoder for 40 Transformer layers total. Under CED, the decoder’s global KV cache is built by projecting the encoder’s final hidden states, instead of being computed from each decoder layer’s hidden states as it normally would be. As a result, only 8B parameters are active per token during prefill and 16B during decode , which cuts costs significantly for agentic workloads that process a lot of input. ￼ DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash builds on Compressed Sparse Attention 2 (CSA2) , where every attention layer runs in one of three fixed modes - Full , Reindex , or Reuse - letting layers share main KV, share indexer K, and recycle Top-K sparse-attention indices. In the decoder, a Hierarchical Sparse Indexer caps later indexing layers to a candidate pool built by the first Full Mode layer, so indexer cost at deeper layers stays bounded no matter how long the context gets. Together with FP4 main KV caching (E2M1 values, one E4M3 scale per 16 channels), this brings the global KV cache down to 890 bytes per token - about a quarter of DeepSeek-V4-Flash. models.description: Readme This model is hosted in the United States and Europe. Like all other models on Ollama’s cloud, this model follows Ollama’s privacy policy with zero data retention. GLM-5.3-Flash is the first natively multimodal model in Z.ai’s GLM-5 series. With 320B total parameters and just 18B active, it outperforms GLM-5.2 across benchmarks and real-world workloads at one-tenth the cost, while approaching Claude Opus 4.8 on coding and agentic benchmarks. Before release, Z.ai tested GLM-5.3-Flash anonymously as ox-alpha where it became the most popular model of the week. Key Features Agentic Coding : Built for sustained, multi-step coding in agent harnesses. Long Context : A 1M context window holds project-scale codebases and long-running sessions. Flexible Thinking : Reasoning is always on, with effort tunable per request across low, high, and max levels. Multimodal Input : Accepts image and video alongside text, for workflows that mix code with visual context. MIT Licensed Competitive performance at Flash cost Across six coding and agentic benchmarks, GLM-5.3-Flash consistently outperforms GLM-5.2, often by a wide margin: 63.4 vs. 46.2 on DeepSWE v1.1 and 48.8 vs. 26.2 on AutomationBench, while approaching Claude Opus 4.8 overall. On the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v4.1.1, it pushes the Pareto frontier at 57 points, a level of intelligence previously only available at roughly 10× the cost per task. The same holds on Z.ai Code Bench v1.0 (run in Claude Code 2.1.207), where GLM-5.3-Flash beats GLM-5.2 at every effort level and, at Max effort, nearly matches Claude Opus 4.8 (29.0 vs. 29.5). Built for efficient inference GLM-5.3-Flash starts from a newly trained base model, with its architecture and training recipe redesigned around capability and efficiency. Compared with GLM-4.5, it has a similar total parameter count (320B vs. 355B) but nearly halves both the active parameters (18B vs. 32B) and the number of layers (45 vs. 92). models.name: pplx-decider-flash is a 4B decision model from Perplexity, built on Qwen3.5-4B
models.description: Readme pplx-decider-flash is a 4B decision model from Perplexity, built on Qwen3.5-4B and distilled from the pplx-decider models: the same request format and the same text and image support, at about one seventh of the size. Give it a state (text, JSON, or images) and a set of typed questions, and it returns a calibrated probability for every answer in a single forward pass. It doesn’t generate text. It’s compatible with the Jev and System One APIs, so it works through Ollama’s /v1/systemone endpoint and ollama run --ask . ollama pull pplx-decider-flash Highlights Most of the accuracy, a fraction of the size : Perplexity’s evaluation puts it at 58.88 overall on the Decision Index 0.3 (60.05 with one question per request) and 72.53 on the vision suite, against 68.09 and 77.43 for pplx-decider. Built for latency : Perplexity positions it for cases where latency or cost matters more than the last points of accuracy. Multimodal : decide over text, JSON, or images such as screenshots, receipts, and forms. One forward pass : every option of every question is scored together, with no output tokens. Apache 2.0 license What you can build Task You define You get back Route a request The destinations and when each applies The chosen destination and each destination’s probability Check a condition A yes or no question True or false, and the probability of each Grade an answer A rubric of levels The probability-weighted level and each level’s probability Gate an agent step A condition and the agent’s proposed action Go or no-go, with the probability of each CLI ollama run pplx-decider-flash --ask "Is a refund being requested?" < ticket.txt ollama run pplx-decider-flash --ask "Which team should handle this?" \ --choice billing="Payments and refunds" \ --choice technical="Outages and errors" < ticket.txt ollama run pplx-decider-flash --ask "How urgent is this?" \ --level "Routine" \ --level "Soon" \ --level "Immediate" < ticket.txt The state can also follow the model name instead

models.description: Readme Kimi K3.1 Pro is an open-weight, natively multimodal agentic model, and our most capable 3T-class model to date. Post-trained from Kimi K3 with large-scale joint reinforcement learning across hundreds of downstream domains, it is the first model in the K3.1 series. With a 1-million-token context window, Kimi K3.1 Pro delivers substantial improvements in coding, 3D creation, financial research, factual accuracy, and other agentic capabilities. Key Features Efficient Long-Context Architecture : Kimi K3.1 Pro keeps Kimi K3’s 2.8T-parameter MoE design, activating 16 of 896 experts (104B active parameters), and replaces full-attention layers with Gated DeepSeek Sparse Attention for more efficient long-context modeling. Long-Horizon Coding : Kimi K3.1 Pro sustains long engineering sessions, from quick fixes to full-project builds, with stronger game development and script-driven 3D modeling in tools like Blender, CAD software and Unity. Financial Research & Factual Accuracy : Kimi K3.1 Pro handles financial modeling, research and business operations, with improved factual accuracy over Kimi K3. Native Multimodality & Long Context : Kimi K3.1 Pro understands text and images, and supports a 1-million-token context window. Open Frontier Weights : We release the full Kimi K3.1 Pro model weights under the Kimi K3.1 Pro License. models.name: Thinking Machines' small open-weights model that can run on a Mac: 26B parameters, 5.4B active, with looped layers for more computation per token.
models.description: Readme Inkling 2 Mini is a small open-weights model from Thinking Machines, small enough to run on a Mac with 32GB+ memory. It has 26B parameters with 5.4B active per token, and loops its middle layers so it does more computation on each token instead of writing more tokens. It’s built for coding, agentic workflows such as computer use, design work that relies on strong visual reasoning, and finance tasks. Get started ollama run inkling-2-mini Key features Runs locally: 26B parameters with 5.4B active per token; runs on a Mac with 32GB+ memory or a DGX Spark. Looping: 12 of its 24 layers run three times per token, so it does more computation on each token instead of writing more tokens. Built for real work: coding, agentic workflows such as finance, computer use, and design with strong visual reasoning. Native 4-bit: trained in NVFP4 and shipped in the same precision, so there’s no quantization loss. Open weights: Apache 2.0. Benchmarks Inkling 2 Mini scores high on coding (79.2% on SWE-Bench Verified, 48.2% on DeepSWE), tool use for agents (82.7% on MCP Atlas) and deep research (85.3% on DeepSearchQA). Inkling 2 Mini also has strong visual reasoning for computer use and design : 76.5% on ScreenSpot Pro (finding things on a screen) and 92.8% on OmniDocBench (reading documents).
